title: Feature file v2.4.0
description: `features/<name>/feature.json`: the committed assignment `workflow launch <name>` prepares. `workers` declares every lane: a node id that must match a `workers[].node_id` of the policy file and the task file that lane receives. `launch --workers a,b` selects a subset; omitted means every declared lane. 2.1.0 adds the optional `reviewers`: every reviewer of the run with its brief (a file relative to the feature directory, existing and non-empty, or `builtin:<id>` for a brief bundled in `workflow/prompts/reviewers/`); a file without `reviewers` runs the single built-in reviewer (`workflow/prompts/review.md`) with id `review`. A 1.0.0 file (`ui_task`/`adapter_task`) is refused by `launch` with a message to use 2.x. Hand-written; the controller validates it with `workflow.verification.validate_schema("feature", ...)` and additionally requires unique node ids, the same id set as the policy, existing non-empty task and brief files inside the feature directory, unique reviewer ids that are neither a lane id nor a reserved name, and version 2.1.0 or later whenever `reviewers` is present. 2.2.0 turns on the guardrails (docs/PRD_PORTABLE_WORKFLOW.md section 4.3): every task must have non-empty `## Goal`, `## Acceptance` and `## Stop` sections, the feature directory must hold a non-empty `decisions.md`, and `prd` must exist in the target; it adds the optional `challenge` (default true: a design challenge runs before any worker) and `prd`. 2.3.0 keeps every 2.2.0 guardrail and adds the optional `sidecar` (docs/PRD_REVIEW_SIDECAR.md section 3): a review sidecar that reads the lanes' diffs and panes on a cadence and on every claimed completion during the work phase, keeps `<run>/sidecar.ledger.json` (contracts/workflow/sidecar.schema.json) and may message a lane through the controller; `false` or an absent key means none, and `sidecar` on an earlier version is refused. `launch` additionally requires a `prompt` file inside the feature directory that exists and is not empty, or a `builtin:<id>` bundled in `workflow/prompts/sidecar/`. 2.4.0 keeps every 2.3.0 rule and adds the optional `critical` (default false), which the workflow-grill skill sets when the operator confirms that the feature's code is critical: an automatic run then stops after review for the operator's `approve`, under any profile; `critical` on an earlier version is refused. 2.4.0 also adds the optional `tryout` (default false): a user-facing feature the operator tries before the merge to main, and that counts toward the untried-feature limit; `tryout` on an earlier version is refused. 2.0.0 and 2.1.0 files launch as before, with a note that no guardrail is enforced; 2.2.0 and 2.3.0 files launch unchanged.

policy.description: Policy file relative to the feature directory (contracts/workflow/verification.schema.json).

node_id.description: A lane id as the policy declares it: lower-case, at most 32 characters, never a reserved graph name, attribution or per-lane prefix.

task.description: Task file relative to the feature directory.

reviewers.description: 2.1.0: the reviewers the review node launches in parallel over the same candidate, in declared order. Each reviewer owns the node `review-<reviewer_id>` and the files `review-<reviewer_id>.*`.

reviewer_id.description: Lower-case, at most 32 characters, unique, never a lane id of the policy nor a reserved graph name, attribution or per-lane prefix.

prompt.description: Brief file relative to the feature directory, or `builtin:<id>` for a bundled brief (workflow/prompts/reviewers/<id>.md); it replaces the built-in brief and states only what to look for (the controller appends the bundle paths, task locations, lane vocabulary and completion protocol).

challenge.description: 2.2.0: run the design challenge node before any worker launch (default true). `false` records the challenge as disabled and the run's graph has no challenge node.

prd.description: 2.2.0: the specification the design challenge reads, a path relative to the target repository that must exist.

critical.description: 2.4.0: the operator confirmed at the grill that this feature's code is critical (default false). `true` pins an automatic run's finish to `approval`: it stops after review until the operator approves.

tryout.description: 2.4.0: a user-facing feature the operator tries before the merge to main (default false). `true` pins `plan.tryout` at prepare: each integrated run waits for `python -m workflow tryout <run> --result works|broken|skipped --by operator`, and a new tryout launch stops while 3 other features wait for theirs (`--allow-untried "<reason>" --by operator` overrides).

sidecar.description: 2.3.0: the review sidecar. `false` (or no key) means none. The bounds are pinned into `plan.sidecar` at prepare with the defaults shown: one pass every `cadence_seconds` and at once when a lane writes a `completed` completion, each a read-only `claude --print` job stopped after `pass_timeout_seconds`, at most `max_passes` passes plus the final pass, and at most `max_messages_per_lane` messages typed into each lane's pane.

prompt.description: The brief: a file relative to the feature directory (existing, non-empty) or `builtin:<id>` for a brief bundled in `workflow/prompts/sidecar/` (today `senior-review`). The controller appends the run's vocabulary, the pass inputs, the ledger and the output rules.
